prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The Green Party’s 2005 manifesto sets out a transformative, justice-first programme that puts people and planet before short‑term profit, replacing privatisation and globalisation with public service, localisation and sustainability.

Economy: Tackle insecurity and inequality by treating nature as “natural capital,” shifting tax from labour and small firms to wealth and resource use. Introduce progressive income bands (e.g., 50% over £50k; 60% over £100k), more corporation tax bands (40% on profits >£1.5m), a progressive inheritance tax on recipients, abolish National Insurance and phase out VAT in favour of revenue‑neutral eco‑taxes. Pilot a locally set Land Value Tax to replace Council Tax and Uniform Business Rates. Localise economies via community banks, credit unions, local currencies; back small co‑ops; oppose UK entry to the euro. Strengthen workers’ rights and reduce working hours. Replace GDP with measures of genuine well‑being.

Climate and energy: Adopt Contraction and Convergence with UK CO2 cuts of 20% by 2010, 50% by 2020, 85% by 2030; expand carbon trading within that framework. Replace VAT and the Climate Change Levy with a Carbon Tax; abolish standing charges and protect low users. Deliver 40% renewable energy by 2020, invest in solar, wind, wave and biogas; launch a Warmer Homes Act and Smart Energy Councils. Close the nuclear programme and redirect R&D to renewables.

Welfare: Create universal, empowering support via a phased Citizen’s Income (replacing most means‑testing) and a Citizen’s Pension (at least at Pension Credit level, linked to earnings, without means‑tests). Simplify family support, raise Child Benefit, curb excessive working hours and expand Sure Start. Boost affordable housing through council housebuilding, self‑build co‑ops, LVT reform and deep retrofit.

Health and education: Restore the NHS to universal, comprehensive care, ending marketisation, PPPs and GATS encroachment. Abolish prescription, eye test and dental charges; expand mental health and preventative care; raise funding to ~9% of GNP with a dedicated NHS Tax. In education, increase funding, scrap tuition fees and restore maintenance grants; abolish SATs and shift to Individual Learning Plans; expand Children’s Centres.

Transport: Cut demand and prioritise walking, cycling, rail and buses; shift £30bn from roads, target a 10% traffic reduction by 2010, re‑regulate buses, and bring rail and tube back to public ownership. Price the real costs of motoring and back efficient vehicles. Curb aviation growth: resist airport expansion, tax aviation fuel EU‑wide, levy domestic flight emissions, raise Air Passenger Duty, ban night flights, and shift short‑haul to rail.

Environment, food, farming: Deliver a Zero Waste Strategy (ban incineration, 60% recycling by 2010), new eco‑taxes and an Environmental Protection Commission; apply the precautionary principle, end patents on life, strengthen animal welfare (end live exports, battery eggs, fur; replace vivisection). Localise food: Organics Target Bill (30% by 2012), abolish CAP/CFP in favour of biodiversity and fair farm incomes, ban GM, and restrain supermarket power.

Crime and democracy: Prevent crime by rebuilding community life, youth services and public spaces; treat drugs as a health issue; expand community policing; enact robust gun controls; embed restorative justice; defend human rights. Renew democracy: oppose ID cards; devolve power and finance (via LVT); introduce PR for councils and Westminster; elect the Lords; enable recalls and local referenda; draft a written constitution with disestablished church and curtailed monarchy.

International: Pursue an ethical, law‑based foreign policy; withdraw from Iraq in favour of UN peacekeepers; cut defence to the EU average; decommission UK nuclear weapons; support a binding Arms Trade Treaty. Exceed UN aid targets (1% of GNI), cancel debts for the 52 poorest countries, and back a Tobin tax. Democratise the UN, IMF and World Bank. Reform trade by replacing/overhauling the WTO with a General Agreement on Sustainable Trade that prioritises localisation, rights and ecology. Uphold asylum rights, including benefits, work and independent appeals, and ratify the UN Migrant Workers Convention.
